todos.text: S8 wording: \enquote{takes effect only in the state on which its guard was evaluated} describes case~(c) of \cref{def:fresh-guard} only. Cases (a) and (b) accept a guard proved against an earlier state, by design, so the sentence is false for the mechanism you define. Write instead: \enquote{A guarded update takes effect only in a state where its guard still holds; if the guard may have become false since it was evaluated, the update is rejected.} The example holds when nothing else touches the group in between; in general at most one reservation succeeds, and both are rejected if an issuance into the group comes first. Checked in the Lean model (\texttt{verification/lean} in the code repository): \texttt{s8\_guarded\_update}, \texttt{stale\_stable\_guard}, \texttt{stale\_volatile\_guard}, \texttt{alice\_bob}, \texttt{both\_rejected}.

S7 wording: \enquote{must be proved against the current state} is too strong. By case~(b) of \cref{def:fresh-guard}, a proof over groups stays acceptable while the versions of those groups do not change, even after other updates. Alice's proof in the example is rejected only because her group also contains Bob's credential; say so. Suggested: \enquote{A statement that can become false is accepted only if the part of the state it depends on has not changed since it was proved.} Checked in the Lean model (\texttt{verification/lean} in the code repository): \texttt{s7\_freshness}, \texttt{stale\_volatile\_guard}.

Missing claim: what the version is for. Add S11 \emph{Authenticated history}: versions only grow, the state that belongs to a version never changes as the log grows, and the current accumulator values encode the state at the current version. Holders refresh their witnesses against past values, and case~(a) proofs bind to past states, through it. Checked in the Lean model (\texttt{verification/lean} in the code repository): \texttt{s11\_history}, \texttt{global\_version}.

todos.text: Fresh values: the first reason holds for issuance only. For a revocation, the step check and the consistency check of \cref{sec:plain-comparison} already tie the new $A$ and $\tilde{R}$ to the stored values, so values computed from an older state fail them. Nothing ties a new $I$ to the stored one: add an issuance check $e(I', \tilde{g}) = e(I, \tilde{g}^{y} \cdot \tilde{Q})$ and drop \cref{def:fresh-values}, or keep the version check and say it guards issuance only. Either way the global version stays, for guards and for the authenticated history. Checked in the Lean model (\texttt{verification/lean} in the code repository): \texttt{stale\_values}, \texttt{issue\_check\_needed}, \texttt{checks\_exact}.

Acceptance rule: the definition \enquote{Accepted update} and the soundness lemma for fresh values are commented out, so the text never says when the \gls{vdr} accepts an update. Bring back a definition: the sender is the issuer, the new values pass the step, consistency and revoked-$\subseteq$-issued checks of \cref{sec:plain-comparison} (and an issuance check), and the guard, if any, is fresh. This is the rule the Lean model (\texttt{verification/lean} in the code repository) checks against: \texttt{s1\_single\_writer}, \texttt{s5\_log\_bound}, \texttt{honest\_update}.

Checks and updates: nothing connects these checks to \cref{def:accumulator-updates}. State a lemma: for an enabled update, the step, consistency and revoked-$\subseteq$-issued checks, with an issuance check, accept exactly the values the accumulator updates compute from the stored values. Also say which update runs which check. Each check is needed: switching one off breaks S2, S3 or S6. Checked in the Lean model (\texttt{verification/lean} in the code repository): \texttt{checks\_exact}, \texttt{honest\_update}, \texttt{step\_check\_needed}, \texttt{consistency\_check\_needed}, \texttt{subset\_check\_needed}, \texttt{issue\_check\_needed}.

Proof: checked in the Lean model (\texttt{verification/lean} in the code repository) as \texttt{representation} in \texttt{Lifecycle/Vdr.lean}. Its steps: update by update and set by set. Lean reads $A$ as the to-do above says: its value encodes $\mathit{Rev}$ (static add) and does not change on issuance, and the set a holder can prove membership in is still $\mathit{Iss} \setminus \mathit{Rev}$; the statement holds.

judgment.note: S4 makes the ordered list of revoked identifiers public, and check (9) needs y in the clear; S9 says an identifier is known only to its issuer and holder. After a revocation both cannot hold. A rewording of S9 as unlinkability (the identifier never appears in a presentation; a revoked identifier in the log cannot be linked to its holder) keeps the privacy goal. Not expressible in the set model, so not kernel-checked.

lem:closure covers quantifiers over conditions only, not Q x in D. Phi with a formula body; the claim that the class of every formula follows from its structure then relies on the fallback 'otherwise volatile'. The Lean theorem proves the lemma as stated; the gap is in coverage.

S2 says an identifier is unique when issued. At group level no pairing check rejects issuing the same y twice (the factor (y+alpha) would repeat in I); uniqueness rests on choosing identifiers at random. The set model folds freshness into the issuance check, which the paper does not have yet.

judgment.topic: Case (a) as an implementation decides it
judgment.note: The model decides case (a) by semantic stability. A contract can only classify a formula by its structure (lem:closure), which accepts fewer guards. A stricter VDR's run equals this VDR's run on the transactions it accepted, so the safety claims should carry over; that argument is not proved.

On an EVM chain a rejected update reverts; the receipt (status 0) is public, and the sender pays the gas used up to the revert (on a rollup also the L1 data fee). Under S1 only the issuer submits, so the issuer pays for contention; a free eth_call pre-check narrows the race window but does not close it. In Fabric an MVCC conflict costs nothing. A possible discussion point; no claim.
